title: fix(memory): session sync deletes and re-embeds every indexed chunk as transcripts grow
body:
Related: #40919

## What Problem This Solves

Growing session transcripts rewrite every indexed chunk on each sync. With the embedding cache disabled, they also send unchanged text to the embedding provider again, spending local CPU/GPU time on repeated work.

## User Impact

Session appends retain unchanged chunk rows and embeddings. Only new or changed chunks are embedded and published, including when caching is disabled. Truncation and provenance changes still take effect; full rebuilds retain complete replacement.

No user configuration, database schema, row encoding, chunk identity, or migration changes. Existing indexes remain usable. Full transcript preparation still occurs; this fixes embedding and publication amplification.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delta publication stays inside the existing SQLite worker. Retained rows are staged first and validated transactionally before indexed writes. Missing rows cause one full-source retry after releasing the workspace lock. Both indexing paths share preparation and recovery. The existing lazy chunk writer owns provenance updates, and vector cleanup/rebuild debt retain their existing owner. Empty sources preserve the optimization from #146150.

Main was merged without rebasing or replacing @wr-web's commits. The branch consumes main's timeout, batch-retry, embedding-format, and admitted-table helpers. The latest conflict resolution moves the kernel to the shared SQLite `tableExists` helper; its delta logic is unchanged. The canonical test fixture now honors `cacheEnabled: false`, which previously fell back to enabled caching and masked provider work.

Production: +376/-123 (net +253, down from the original +326). Tests/support: +310/-2. Docs: +3/-0. Tooling: one stale max-lines exemption removed. Neutral production would require unrelated deletion or dropping staged transfer, drift recovery, or publication safeguards.

## Evidence

Final head: `2bb17071d149f380cdb10ceee516994c9d74d928`. Integrated main: `51e7ca28cb945c522ad7e1ca994790fba5eeed12`. Runtime proof uses `3b60992c552e23017e87b99b2b967cabc6cdb4c9`; the sole later change removes the stale baseline entry.

Real CLI → Memory Core → publication worker → Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, behind a loopback logging proxy on macOS/Node 26.11.1. Synthetic 100-turn session, then two appended turns. The candidate used a copy of main's existing index; cache disabled for this comparison:

| Measurement after two appended turns | Main (`c75ff3cbf56e`) | Candidate runtime |
|---|---:|---:|
| Indexed chunks | 29 | 29 |
| Embedding requests | 6 | 1 |
| Embedded inputs | 29 | 1 |
| Unchanged rows kept untouched | 0/28 | 28/28 |
| Index revision | 30 → 89 | 30 → 33 |

All embedding requests succeeded. The default-cache control on main sent one input, showing that caching hides provider work but not row churn. Current main still clears/replaces the source rows. The candidate index completed in 37.42s; early/latest searches took 20.90s/25.36s and returned the correct retained and updated ranges without stale warnings. The latest top-result range 198–205 contains the appended turns.

The corrected replay preserves the baseline config byte for byte, including the proxy address. An earlier fixture restart changed that address, correctly invalidated the endpoint-scoped provider key, and forced a full rebuild. That run is excluded from delta proof; no product code was changed for the fixture error.

```sh
# OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH point to isolated synthetic state.
pnpm openclaw --profile memory-sync memory index --verbose
pnpm openclaw --profile memory-sync memory search topic-001 --max-results 5 --min-score 0 --json
pnpm openclaw --profile memory-sync memory search topic-102 --max-results 5 --min-score 0 --json
```

Validation:

- Corrected session-delta regression fails on main at retained-row equality: 157.09s wall.
- Final integration: eight focused files, 103/103 tests via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`, 777.40s command wall (720.70s Vitest). Test callback totals: session-delta 12.054s, publication-transfer 13.572s, source-kernel 0.679s, vector-state 0.046s, targeted-sync 0.029s, index-retention 17.632s, existing reindex-recovery 197.377s and startup-catchup 95.225s. The owning-boundary regression exercises real manager preparation, native session storage, worker publication, and provider-input exclusion. The earlier nine-file 170/170 run remains evidence for unchanged probe, timeout-policy, and shadow-owner behavior.
- Full `pnpm build`: pass, 2338.01s. Production/test types: pass, 57.38s/54.16s. Scoped oxlint: pass, 934.44s including declaration preparation under the supported budget. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Assertion-safety, max-lines, line-cap, database-worker, test-timeout-race, test-mock-exports, config-doc, and plugin-inventory checks pass. Max-lines initially found the same stale doctor-test exemption present in pinned main; that test is 877 lines in both main and candidate. Removing only the obsolete exemption made the check pass in 80.56s. No baseline growth or test-timeout increase.
- Exact-head CI run `38042571477` passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its three changed-extension test bundles took 242–255s each, 742 aggregate job-seconds including setup and sibling tests; this is not isolated regression cost. ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head: 5/6, proof sufficient, no findings or Before merge items.
- Fresh Codex autoreview of the final head: scoped-clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable finding. Hosted review and CI are checked against the pushed head separately.

Builds and tests were serialized after an earlier attempt collided with generated package artifacts. Proof files and logs distinguish that tooling failure, the changed-route fixture, and the passing runs.
